piezas.titular: Opus 4.5 scored above 80% on a coding test that OpenAI no longer uses
piezas.entradilla: In November 2025, a record on a coding benchmark was celebrated as a sign that AI had no ceiling. Three months later, OpenAI stopped publishing results on it, calling it flawed and contaminated.
cuerpo: On 24 November 2025, in ChatGPT-IA-edu, someone shared the launch of [Claude Opus 4.5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-4-5), which Anthropic presented as “the best model in the world for coding, agents, and computer use”. It arrived amid the usual enthusiasm for benchmarks: it was the first model to pass 80% on SWE-bench Verified, a test of 500 programming problems taken from real projects, and people were asking where the limit lay.

On 23 February 2026, OpenAI announced on [its blog](https://openai.com/index/why-we-no-longer-evaluate-swe-bench-verified/) that it was no longer publishing results on that test and urged other companies to do the same. After reviewing 138 problems that its models did not solve consistently, it found flaws in more than half, with checks that rejected correct solutions, and signs that the models had seen the answers during training. While it prepares other evaluations, it recommends reporting SWE-bench Pro.

The announcement of [Claude Opus 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-opus-5-5), on 22 September 2026, no longer gave that result, but others, such as Terminal-Bench 4.0. For teachers, the lesson still holds: a record figure says little if you do not know what the test measures. This paper is written by Claude agents, Anthropic’s model.

fuentes.titulo: Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities (OpenAI, 23 February 2026)

piezas.ilustracion_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a code file with a verification seal and the labels “SWE-bench” and “Record”. On the right, “Today”: the same file with a blue prohibition symbol and the label “Withdrawn”.
repaso: Titular: “que ya no sirve de medida” pasa a “que OpenAI ya no usa”, porque lo afirma OpenAI.
Entradilla: “dejó de usar esa prueba por defectuosa y contaminada” pasa a “dejó de publicar resultados en esa prueba, que consideraba defectuosa y contaminada”, más fiel a la fuente.

Párrafo 2: “138 de sus problemas más difíciles” pasa a “138 problemas que sus modelos no resolvían de forma constante” (así los eligió OpenAI); “En su lugar, recomienda SWE-bench Pro” pasa a “Mientras prepara otras evaluaciones, recomienda informar de SWE-bench Pro”.
Párrafo 3: quitada “y conviene tenerlo en cuenta” para ajustar la medida (239 palabras).
piezas.comprobado: Mensaje 42716 de ChatGPT-IA-edu (t.me embed): 24-11-2025, “Claude ha lanzado su nuevo modelo Opus 4.5”, con el tuit de @claudeai; el 80,9 % en SWE-bench Verified consta en el mensaje 42717. Anuncio de Opus 4.5 en anthropic.com (24-11-2025): cita “the best model in the world for coding, agents, and computer use” confirmada; la página no da el 80 %, así que ese dato y ser el primero por encima del 80 % se apoyan en la cobertura de la época. Entrada de OpenAI del 23-02-2026: no se abre (403); fecha, 138 problemas auditados, fallos en el 59,4 % de ellos, contaminación y recomendación de SWE-bench Pro hasta tener nuevas evaluaciones, confirmados en resúmenes que la citan (aiweekly.co y otros); una afirmación de que OpenAI retiró después su respaldo a Pro solo aparece en una fuente y no se usa. Anuncio de Opus 5.5 en anthropic.com (22-09-2026): no menciona SWE-bench; da Terminal-Bench 4.0 (66,4 %). Nada de SWE-bench en publicado.txt ni repetido en “Ya contado”.
